deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: A policy should be set for this to either be PREVENT or ABANDON as this will prevent a user from accidentally deleting a copy or backup of a disk.

description.description: An optional description of this resource.
description.rationale: A description of the resource. This is a reference and therefore does not affect the security.

labels.description:
Labels to apply to this InstantSnapshot.

**Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the labels present in your configuration.
Please refer to the field 'effective_labels' for all of the labels present on the resource.
labels.rationale: A label of the resource does not affect the security as this label is for labels under your configuration and not server wide.

name.description:
Name of the resource; provided by the client when the resource is
created. The name must be 1-63 characters long, and comply with
RFC1035. Specifically, the name must be 1-63 characters long and match
the regular expression '[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?' which means the
first character must be a lowercase letter, and all following
characters must be a dash, lowercase letter, or digit, except the last
character, which cannot be a dash.
name.rationale: The name of the resource does not affect the security of the resource or its backup.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: The project ID is just a identifier for the instant snapshot and therefore does not have any security impact.

source_disk.description: A reference to the disk used to create this instant snapshot.
source_disk.rationale: This is a reference to the disk that is used to create the instant snapshot, data residency is enforced on google_compute_disk and therefore this has no security implications.

zone.description: A reference to the zone where the disk is located.
zone.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

params.description: Additional params passed with the request, but not persisted as part of resource payload

params.resource_manager_tags.description:
Resource manager tags to be bound to the instant snapshot. Tag keys and values have the
same definition as resource manager tags. Keys must be in the format tagKeys/{tag_key_id},
and values are in the format tagValues/456.
params.resource_manager_tags.rationale: Resource manager tags are organisational metadata used for categorisation, cost attribution, and as optional keys for conditional IAM bindings. The tags themselves grant no access and enforce no control; any security effect depends entirely on organisation-specific IAM conditions or org policies defined elsewhere. A generic platform policy does not know which tag keys a given organisation uses or mandate their presence without overreaching into team-specific resource organisation.
